---
title: Spark Column Lineage Coverage
description: How the column lineage Invaract publishes for Spark jobs compares with openlineage-spark and Spline, construct by construct, measured on real jobs.
---

<!-- Generated by lineage-crosscheck (LineageCrossCheckSpec; run with CROSSCHECK_UPDATE=true to regenerate). Do not edit by hand. -->

Invaract publishes column lineage for Spark jobs in its [OpenLineage events](/guides/openlineage/), traced from the
job's analyzed plan. This page shows how complete and correct that lineage is. Each of the 55 Spark jobs below runs once,
with three tools capturing lineage from the same run: Invaract, [openlineage-spark](https://openlineage.io/docs/integrations/spark/)
(OpenLineage's own Spark integration) and the [Spline](https://absaoss.github.io/spline/) agent. Versions measured:
openlineage-spark 1.55.0, Spline agent 2.4.0, Spark 3.5.9. For each job's write, the comparison covers:

- **datasets**: the input and output datasets, named by the [OpenLineage naming conventions](https://openlineage.io/docs/spec/naming);
- **direct lineage**: which input columns each output column's value comes from, and how (`IDENTITY`,
  `TRANSFORMATION`, `AGGREGATION`, masking);
- **indirect lineage**: which input columns decide the output's rows or their order (`FILTER`, `JOIN`, `GROUP_BY`,
  `SORT`), or which value an output column takes (`CONDITIONAL`, `WINDOW`).

Spline does not classify edges, so against Spline every column an output column depends on is compared, by value or not.

Invaract agrees with openlineage-spark on 35 of 55 jobs, and with Spline on
41 of 55. A job agrees only when every dataset and every edge, with its type, is the same;
each difference is listed below with its reason. Most come from one of two things: openlineage-spark reads Spark's
*optimized* plan, so it also reports columns the optimizer added (such as an `isnotnull` filter on a join key); or
another tool misses part of the plan Invaract follows ([what Invaract captures that the others
miss](#what-invaract-captures-that-the-others-miss)). The rest are conventions, and [Invaract's known gaps](#known-gaps).

## Check it yourself

Everything on this page comes from one run of the `lineage-crosscheck` module, and the code shown for each job is the
code that ran. To run it, from a checkout of Invaract with Java 11 or later and sbt:

```bash
./dev/build                        # builds Invaract and publishes it locally
cd lineage-crosscheck && sbt test  # runs every job under all three tools and compares them
```

The run fails when any job's lineage, Invaract's or a reference's, differs from what is recorded here
(`lineage-crosscheck/src/test/resources/crosscheck-baseline.txt`). CI runs it on every pull request and every push,
so lineage verified here cannot change without the change being reviewed. After an intended change, explain it in
`Corpus.scala` and run `CROSSCHECK_UPDATE=true sbt test` to rewrite the baseline and this page.

In the code, `s` is the job's `SparkSession` and `f` the shared inputs: `f.orders(s)` and `f.customers(s)` read
Parquet, `f.events(s)` JSON. A job that is a DataFrame expression is written as Parquet to `out`.

| Input | Format | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `orders` | Parquet | `id`, `customer_id`, `amount`, `status` |
| `customers` | Parquet | `customer_id`, `name`, `country`, `email` |
| `events` | JSON | `id`, `payload` (a struct of `a` and `b`), `tags` (an array) |
| `sales.csv` | CSV | `region`, `amount` |
| `ACCOUNTS` | H2, over JDBC | `ID`, `BALANCE` |

In the lineage, `<in>` is the inputs' directory and `<out>` the job's own. `field <- dataset.column` is direct
lineage, `field <~ dataset.column` indirect (`*`: on every row of the output), each with its OpenLineage type.

## Summary

| Spark construct | Job | openlineage-spark | Spline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Projection | a subset of the input's columns (`select`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Projection | a column renamed (`rename`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Projection | a column computed from two others (`arithmetic`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Projection | withColumn replacing an existing column (`with-column-replace`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Projection | coalesce, concat and a cast over several columns (`functions`) | [differs](#functions): a convention | ✓ agrees |
| Projection | a constant column and the current time beside an input column (`literal`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Conditional | CASE WHEN: the value from one column, chosen by another (`case-when`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Projection | a hash of a column (sha2), which OpenLineage marks as masking (`masking`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Filter | rows kept by a condition on a column not written (`filter`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Sort | top rows by a column (`sort-limit`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Deduplication | distinct rows (`distinct`) | ✓ agrees | [differs](#distinct): the other tool's limit |
| Deduplication | dropDuplicates on a subset of columns (`drop-duplicates`) | ✓ agrees | [differs](#drop-duplicates): the other tool's limit |
| Join | an inner join, columns from both sides (`inner-join`) | [differs](#inner-join): the other tool's limit | ✓ agrees |
| Join | a left join on two conditions (`left-join`) | [differs](#left-join): the other tool's limit | ✓ agrees |
| Join | a table joined with itself under two aliases (`self-join`) | [differs](#self-join): the other tool's limit | ✓ agrees |
| Aggregation | sum, count and max by a key (`group-by`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Aggregation | count(*) over the whole input (`global-aggregate`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Aggregation | a join, a filter and an aggregate of an expression (`join-aggregate`) | [differs](#join-aggregate): the other tool's limit | ✓ agrees |
| Window | row_number over a partition, ordered (`window`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Window | a running sum over a window (`window-aggregate`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Aggregation | a pivot of one column's values into columns (`pivot`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Aggregation | rollup over two keys (`rollup`) | [differs](#rollup): the other tool's limit | [differs](#rollup): the other tool's limit |
| Set operation | a union of two inputs' columns (`union`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Nested data | a field of a struct column (`nested-field`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Nested data | a struct built from two columns (`struct-build`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Nested data | explode of an array column (`explode`) | [differs](#explode): the other tool's limit | ✓ agrees |
| SQL | SQL over a temporary view (`sql-view`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| SQL | a CTE referenced twice (`sql-cte`) | [differs](#sql-cte): the other tool's limit | [differs](#sql-cte): the other tool's limit |
| SQL | a filter by IN (subquery) over another input (`in-subquery`) | [differs](#in-subquery): the other tool's limit | [differs](#in-subquery): the other tool's limit |
| SQL | a filter by EXISTS (correlated subquery) (`exists-subquery`) | [differs](#exists-subquery): the other tool's limit | [differs](#exists-subquery): the other tool's limit |
| SQL | a scalar subquery in the select list (`scalar-subquery`) | [differs](#scalar-subquery): the other tool's limit | [differs](#scalar-subquery): the other tool's limit |
| UDF | a Scala UDF over two columns (`scala-udf`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Dataset API | a typed map over a Dataset of case classes (`typed-map`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Dataset API | a DataFrame built from an RDD of another input's rows (`rdd`) | ✓ agrees | [differs](#rdd): the other tool's limit |
| Caching | a cached DataFrame, then a projection of it (`cache`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Caching | a projection of a locally checkpointed DataFrame (`local-checkpoint`) | [differs](#local-checkpoint): the other tool's limit | [differs](#local-checkpoint): the other tool's limit |
| Physical | repartition and coalesce between read and write (`repartition`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Formats | a CSV input with a header (`csv-input`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |
| Formats | Parquet and JSON inputs joined (USING: the key is the left side's) (`multiple-inputs`) | [differs](#multiple-inputs): the other tool's limit | ✓ agrees |
| Join | a right join USING a key: the key is the right side's (`using-right-join`) | [differs](#using-right-join): the other tool's limit | ✓ agrees |
| Deduplication | SELECT DISTINCT (`sql-distinct`) | ✓ agrees | [differs](#sql-distinct): the other tool's limit |

| Writes | an append to an existing directory (`append`) | ✓ agrees | ✓ agrees |

## What Invaract captures that the others miss

Jobs where Invaract reports lineage another tool does not, because that tool does not follow that part of the plan.
Each shows the job's code, what Invaract publishes for it, and the lineage each other tool leaves out.

### Distinct rows (`distinct`)

```scala
f.orders(s).select("status").distinct()
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
status <- file:<in>/orders.status  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.status  [INDIRECT/GROUP_BY]
```

Spline leaves out: Spline records no grouping for a deduplication. Invaract, like openlineage-spark, reports the columns it deduplicates on as GROUP_BY: Spark itself turns a deduplication into an aggregate grouped by them.

```text
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.status
```

### DropDuplicates on a subset of columns (`drop-duplicates`)

```scala
f.orders(s).dropDuplicates("customer_id")
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
amount <- file:<in>/orders.amount  [DIRECT/AGGREGATION]
customer_id <- file:<in>/orders.customer_id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
id <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/AGGREGATION]
status <- file:<in>/orders.status  [DIRECT/AGGREGATION]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.customer_id  [INDIRECT/GROUP_BY]
```

Spline leaves out: Spline records no grouping for a deduplication. Invaract, like openlineage-spark, reports the columns it deduplicates on as GROUP_BY: Spark itself turns a deduplication into an aggregate grouped by them.

```text
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.customer_id
```

### Rollup over two keys (`rollup`)

```scala
f.orders(s).rollup("customer_id", "status").agg(sum("amount").as("total"))
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
customer_id <- file:<in>/orders.customer_id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
status <- file:<in>/orders.status  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
total <- file:<in>/orders.amount  [DIRECT/AGGREGATION]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.customer_id  [INDIRECT/GROUP_BY]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.status  [INDIRECT/GROUP_BY]
```

openlineage-spark leaves out: openlineage-spark does not trace a rollup's grouping keys through the Expand Spark computes it with, so it reports no source for them and no grouping. Invaract traces each key to its column.

```text
direct: customer_id <- file:<in>/orders.customer_id
direct: status <- file:<in>/orders.status
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.customer_id
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.status
```

Spline leaves out: Spline does not trace a rollup's grouping keys through Spark's Expand either. Invaract traces each key to its column.

```text
dependency: customer_id <- file:<in>/orders.customer_id
dependency: status <- file:<in>/orders.status
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.customer_id
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.status
```

### A CTE referenced twice (`sql-cte`)

```scala
f.orders(s).createOrReplaceTempView("orders")
s.sql("WITH big AS (SELECT id, customer_id FROM orders WHERE amount > 60) SELECT a.id, b.customer_id FROM big a JOIN big b ON a.id = b.id")
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
customer_id <- file:<in>/orders.customer_id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
id <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.amount  [INDIRECT/FILTER]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.id  [INDIRECT/JOIN]
```

Spline leaves out: Spline traces no column through a CTE referenced twice. Invaract inlines the CTE, as Spark's optimizer does, and traces through it.

```text
dependency: customer_id <- file:<in>/orders.customer_id
dependency: id <- file:<in>/orders.id
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.id
```

### A filter by IN (subquery) over another input (`in-subquery`)

```scala
f.orders(s).createOrReplaceTempView("orders"); f.customers(s).createOrReplaceTempView("customers")
s.sql("SELECT id FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE country = 'uk')")
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/customers
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
id <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
* <~ file:<in>/customers.country  [INDIRECT/FILTER]
* <~ file:<in>/customers.customer_id  [INDIRECT/FILTER]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.customer_id  [INDIRECT/FILTER]
```

Spline leaves out: Spline does not follow a subquery inside a filter: it misses the subquery's input and the columns it filters on.

```text
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/customers.country
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/customers.customer_id
input: file:<in>/customers
```

### A filter by EXISTS (correlated subquery) (`exists-subquery`)

```scala
f.orders(s).createOrReplaceTempView("orders"); f.customers(s).createOrReplaceTempView("customers")
s.sql("SELECT id FROM orders o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM customers c WHERE c.customer_id = o.customer_id)")
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/customers
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
id <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
* <~ file:<in>/customers.customer_id  [INDIRECT/FILTER]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.customer_id  [INDIRECT/FILTER]
```

Spline leaves out: Spline does not follow a subquery inside a filter: it misses the subquery's input and the column it correlates on.

```text
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/customers.customer_id
input: file:<in>/customers
```

### A scalar subquery in the select list (`scalar-subquery`)

```scala
f.orders(s).createOrReplaceTempView("orders"); f.customers(s).createOrReplaceTempView("customers")
s.sql("SELECT id, (SELECT max(customer_id) FROM customers) AS top_customer FROM orders")
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/customers
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
id <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
top_customer <- file:<in>/customers.customer_id  [DIRECT/AGGREGATION]
```

openlineage-spark leaves out: openlineage-spark does not follow a scalar subquery in the select list: it misses the input the subquery reads and the column its value comes from.

```text
direct: top_customer <- file:<in>/customers.customer_id
input: file:<in>/customers
```

Spline leaves out: Spline does not follow a scalar subquery in the select list either.

```text
dependency: top_customer <- file:<in>/customers.customer_id
input: file:<in>/customers
```

### A DataFrame built from an RDD of another input's rows (`rdd`)

```scala
val rows = f.orders(s).rdd
s.createDataFrame(rows, f.orders(s).schema).select("id")
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
```

Spline leaves out: Spline does not look into an RDD for the files it read; Invaract, like openlineage-spark, reports them as the input (with no column traced through the RDD).

```text
input: file:<in>/orders
```

### A projection of a locally checkpointed DataFrame (`local-checkpoint`)

```scala
f.orders(s).localCheckpoint().select(col("id"), col("amount"))
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
amount <- file:<in>/orders.amount  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
id <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
```

openlineage-spark leaves out: openlineage-spark does not see past a localCheckpoint(). Invaract resolves the checkpoint to the plan it was made from and traces through it.

```text
direct: amount <- file:<in>/orders.amount
direct: id <- file:<in>/orders.id
input: file:<in>/orders
```

Spline leaves out: Spline does not see past a localCheckpoint() either.

```text
dependency: amount <- file:<in>/orders.amount
dependency: id <- file:<in>/orders.id
input: file:<in>/orders
```

### SELECT DISTINCT (`sql-distinct`)

```scala
f.orders(s).createOrReplaceTempView("orders")
s.sql("SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, status FROM orders")
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
customer_id <- file:<in>/orders.customer_id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
status <- file:<in>/orders.status  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.customer_id  [INDIRECT/GROUP_BY]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.status  [INDIRECT/GROUP_BY]
```

Spline leaves out: Spline records no grouping for a deduplication. Invaract, like openlineage-spark, reports the columns it deduplicates on as GROUP_BY: Spark itself turns a deduplication into an aggregate grouped by them.

```text
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.customer_id
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.status
```

### MERGE with conditional, DELETE, partial INSERT and NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE clauses (`delta-merge-clauses`)

```scala
f.orders(s).limit(0).select("id", "amount", "status").write.format("delta").save(out.at("out"))
f.orders(s).createOrReplaceTempView("orders")
s.sql(s"MERGE INTO delta.`${out.at("out")}` t USING orders o ON t.id = o.id " +
  "WHEN MATCHED AND o.status = 'cancelled' THEN DELETE " +
  "WHEN MATCHED AND o.amount > t.amount THEN UPDATE SET t.amount = o.amount " +
  "WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, amount) VALUES (o.id, o.amount * 100) " +
  "WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN UPDATE SET t.status = 'gone'")
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
input:  file:<out>/out
output: file:<out>/out
amount <- file:<in>/orders.amount  [DIRECT/IDENTITY, DIRECT/TRANSFORMATION]
amount <- file:<out>/out.amount  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
id <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
id <- file:<out>/out.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
status <- file:<in>/orders.status  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
status <- file:<out>/out.status  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.amount  [INDIRECT/FILTER]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.id  [INDIRECT/JOIN]
* <~ file:<out>/out.amount  [INDIRECT/FILTER]
* <~ file:<out>/out.id  [INDIRECT/JOIN]
```

openlineage-spark leaves out: openlineage-spark does not follow a MERGE's clauses: it reports the amount the INSERT computes (amount * 100) as a copy, misses the table's own amount that the NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE clause keeps, and reports no indirect lineage - neither the ON condition nor the clause conditions that decide which rows are written.

```text
direct: amount <- file:<out>/out.amount
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.amount
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.id
indirect: * <~ file:<out>/out.amount
indirect: * <~ file:<out>/out.id
```

Spline leaves out: Spline records no indirect lineage for a MERGE: neither its ON condition nor the clause conditions that decide which rows are written.

```text
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.amount
indirect: * <~ file:<in>/orders.id
indirect: * <~ file:<out>/out.amount
indirect: * <~ file:<out>/out.id
```

### A file stream into a file sink, run once (availableNow) (`streaming`)

```scala
val q = s.readStream.schema(f.orders(s).schema).parquet(f.orders).select(col("id"), (col("amount") * 3).as("tripled"))
  .writeStream.format("parquet").option("checkpointLocation", out.at("checkpoint"))
  .trigger(org.apache.spark.sql.streaming.Trigger.AvailableNow()).start(out.at("out"))
q.awaitTermination()
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
id <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
tripled <- file:<in>/orders.amount  [DIRECT/TRANSFORMATION]
```

openlineage-spark leaves out: openlineage-spark publishes no dataset for a file stream written to a file sink. Invaract checks a stream once, when it starts, and publishes its lineage then.

```text
direct: id <- file:<in>/orders.id
direct: tripled <- file:<in>/orders.amount
input: file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
```

Spline leaves out: Spline's agent records no lineage for a Structured Streaming query. Invaract checks a stream once, when it starts, and publishes its lineage then.

```text
dependency: id <- file:<in>/orders.id
dependency: tripled <- file:<in>/orders.amount
input: file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
```

### A table read over JDBC (`jdbc-input`)

```scala
s.read.jdbc(f.jdbcUrl, "ACCOUNTS", new java.util.Properties()).select(col("ID").as("id"), col("BALANCE").as("balance"))
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  h2:<in>/bank;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1:ACCOUNTS
output: file:<out>/out
balance <- h2:<in>/bank;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1:ACCOUNTS.BALANCE  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
id <- h2:<in>/bank;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1:ACCOUNTS.ID  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
```

Spline leaves out: Spline cannot parse an H2 file URL and names the table jdbc://:null.

```text
dependency: balance <- h2:<in>/bank;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1:ACCOUNTS.BALANCE
dependency: id <- h2:<in>/bank;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1:ACCOUNTS.ID
input: h2:<in>/bank;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1:ACCOUNTS
```

## Known gaps

None of the jobs on this page shows a gap in Invaract's lineage.

Limits of Invaract's Spark lineage that no job on this page measures:

- **A table its own write creates, in a catalog that chooses where to store it.** Invaract names a table a write
  creates by where it will be stored when Spark's configuration says (a `LOCATION`, the session catalog, an Iceberg
  Hadoop or JDBC catalog). In a catalog that chooses the location when it creates the table (an Iceberg Hive, REST
  or Glue catalog, for example), Invaract names the table by its catalog identifier.
- **Streaming queries.** Invaract checks a streaming query once, when it starts, and publishes that lineage. It
  publishes nothing for each micro-batch.
- **User-defined functions.** A column a UDF computes has the UDF's input columns as its sources, typed
  `TRANSFORMATION` and described as opaque: what the function does with them is not known.
- **RDDs.** A DataFrame made from an RDD has the files the RDD read as its inputs, with no column lineage through
  the RDD.
- **Operators Invaract does not translate.** An operator Invaract does not translate is a boundary: a column
  computed through it has no sources.
- **A MERGE's DELETE clauses, and the rows it leaves.** The rows a DELETE clause removes are not written, so its
  condition is not reported. Rows no clause touches are not counted, as openlineage-spark counts them.

## Every job

### select

Projection: a subset of the input's columns.

```scala
f.orders(s).select("id", "amount")
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
amount <- file:<in>/orders.amount  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
id <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
```

**Against openlineage-spark**: agrees.

**Against Spline**: agrees.

### rename

Projection: a column renamed.

```scala
f.orders(s).select(col("amount").as("total"))
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
total <- file:<in>/orders.amount  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
```

**Against openlineage-spark**: agrees.

**Against Spline**: agrees.

### arithmetic

Projection: a column computed from two others.

```scala
f.orders(s).select(col("id"), (col("amount") * 2 + col("id")).as("score"))
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
output: file:<out>/out
id <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
score <- file:<in>/orders.amount  [DIRECT/TRANSFORMATION]
score <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/TRANSFORMATION]
```

**Against openlineage-spark**: agrees.

**Against Spline**: agrees.

### with-column-replace

Projection: withColumn replacing an existing column.

```scala
f.orders(s).withColumn("amount", col("amount") + 1)
```

Invaract publishes:

### delta-merge

Delta Lake: MERGE INTO a Delta table from another input.

```scala
f.orders(s).limit(0).select("id", "amount").write.format("delta").save(out.at("out"))
f.orders(s).createOrReplaceTempView("orders")
s.sql(s"MERGE INTO delta.`${out.at("out")}` t USING orders o ON t.id = o.id " +
  "WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET t.amount = o.amount WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, amount) VALUES (o.id, o.amount)")
```

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
input:  file:<out>/out
output: file:<out>/out

id <- file:<out>/out.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.id  [INDIRECT/JOIN]
* <~ file:<out>/out.id  [INDIRECT/JOIN]
```

**Against openlineage-spark** (a convention): A MERGE's ON condition decides which rows each of its clauses writes: Invaract reports its columns as INDIRECT/JOIN, as for any join. openlineage-spark reports no indirect lineage for a MERGE.

```text
indirect: only invaract: * <~ file:<in>/orders.id
indirect: only invaract: * <~ file:<out>/out.id
```

**Against Spline** (a convention): Spline also counts the rows a MERGE leaves as they are (no clause touches them), so the table's own amount is a source of amount; Invaract, like openlineage-spark, counts the rows the MERGE's clauses write. Spline records no indirect lineage, so not the ON condition either.

```text

indirect: only invaract: * <~ file:<out>/out.id
```

### delta-merge-clauses

Delta Lake: MERGE with conditional, DELETE, partial INSERT and NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE clauses.

```scala
f.orders(s).limit(0).select("id", "amount", "status").write.format("delta").save(out.at("out"))
f.orders(s).createOrReplaceTempView("orders")
s.sql(s"MERGE INTO delta.`${out.at("out")}` t USING orders o ON t.id = o.id " +
  "WHEN MATCHED AND o.status = 'cancelled' THEN DELETE " +
  "WHEN MATCHED AND o.amount > t.amount THEN UPDATE SET t.amount = o.amount " +
  "WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, amount) VALUES (o.id, o.amount * 100) " +
  "WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN UPDATE SET t.status = 'gone'")
```

Invaract publishes:

```text
input:  file:<in>/orders
input:  file:<out>/out
output: file:<out>/out

amount <- file:<out>/out.amount  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
id <- file:<in>/orders.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
id <- file:<out>/out.id  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
status <- file:<in>/orders.status  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
status <- file:<out>/out.status  [DIRECT/IDENTITY]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.amount  [INDIRECT/FILTER]
* <~ file:<in>/orders.id  [INDIRECT/JOIN]
* <~ file:<out>/out.amount  [INDIRECT/FILTER]
* <~ file:<out>/out.id  [INDIRECT/JOIN]
```

**Against openlineage-spark** (the other tool's limit): openlineage-spark does not follow a MERGE's clauses: it reports the amount the INSERT computes (amount * 100) as a copy, misses the table's own amount that the NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE clause keeps, and reports no indirect lineage - neither the ON condition nor the clause conditions that decide which rows are written.

```text

indirect: only invaract: * <~ file:<in>/orders.amount
indirect: only invaract: * <~ file:<in>/orders.id
indirect: only invaract: * <~ file:<out>/out.amount
indirect: only invaract: * <~ file:<out>/out.id
```

**Against Spline** (the other tool's limit): Spline records no indirect lineage for a MERGE: neither its ON condition nor the clause conditions that decide which rows are written.

```text

indirect: only invaract: * <~ file:<in>/orders.id
indirect: only invaract: * <~ file:<out>/out.amount

```
